# The two loop forms that walk nothing, and the two escapes, in each host
# language. Go has a bare `for`, so both forms are one; Kotlin's `for` takes an
# iterable, so both are a `while`. `break` and `continue` are spelled the same
# in all three, which is why no language carries a hook for them.

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=go app.sngl
exists go/model.go

# Go: the condition goes in the head, and no head at all is `for {`.
grep 'for m.i < m.n \{' go/model.go
grep 'for \{' go/model.go
grep 'continue' go/model.go
grep 'break' go/model.go
# Nothing materialises a sequence to walk: there is no iterable here at all.
! grep 'range' go/model.go

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=web app.sngl
grep 'while \(state.i < state.n\) \{' web/index.html
grep 'while \(true\) \{' web/index.html
grep 'continue;' web/index.html
grep 'break;' web/index.html

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=droid app.sngl
grep 'while \(\(i < n\)\) \{' droid/MainScreen.kt
grep 'while \(true\) \{' droid/MainScreen.kt
grep 'continue' droid/MainScreen.kt
grep 'break' droid/MainScreen.kt

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var n = 6
    var i = 0
    var total = 0

    button(text="run", @click {
        for i < n {
            i = i + 1
            if i % 2 == 0 {
                continue
            }
            total = total + i
        }
        for {
            if total > 100 {
                break
            }
            total = total + total
        }
    })
    text(value=string(total))
}
